title: Uninterrupted electricity supply was set to resume after a 270 MW coal unit returned to service.
body_paragraphs: The National System Operator (the entity that runs the national grid) said scheduled demand management would cease, following restoration works at the plant. It announced the unit’s full load return at 1.31 p.m. and confirmed no further peak‑hour curtailment was required from October 22.

The move came days after an islandwide outage on October 17, when rooftop generators were asked to disconnect and one‑hour evening cuts were implemented from October 19 to 21. Those rotations were published across four groups with 30‑minute restoration buffers, while investigations into the grid trip proceeded on a formal timetable.

title: Draft anti‑terror and organised crime bills faced calls for withdrawal from legal professionals.
body_paragraphs: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka warned that proposed detention and bail provisions would weaken judicial oversight and risk curtailing liberties. It highlighted concerns about executive‑signed detention orders, High Court‑only bail for specified offences and broad definitions that could capture peaceful activity.

Separately, the Speaker reported that 40 petitions had been filed against the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (PSTA, a planned replacement for the PTA), with hearings held before a three‑judge bench. Earlier notices also listed dozens of petitions on the Sri Lanka Cricket Bill, indicating a heavy constitutional docket.

title: A yuan clearing facility was launched in Colombo to settle trade with China directly.
body_paragraphs: Authorised by the People’s Bank of China, the Bank of China’s local branch will act as the clearing bank (a designated bank that settles payments between local banks and a foreign currency system) for cross‑border RMB transactions. The arrangement enables local banks to route payments without converting through US dollars, reducing currency conversion costs and timing risk.

Officials from both countries attended the launch, which the Finance Ministry said would deepen financial links. The facility also seeks to streamline processing between local institutions and Chinese counterparts by providing a domestic settlement channel.

title: Tea export volumes fell 2.9% in September as packet and bulk shipments slipped.
body_paragraphs: Customs data compiled by Forbes & Walker showed shipments at 23.09 million kilogrammes versus 23.78 million a year earlier, while average FOB value (free‑on‑board, a price excluding freight and insurance) rose to US$ 5.85 per kg from US$ 5.76. Over January–September, volumes were down 4.5% to 189.41 million kg and average dollar values eased to US$ 5.73 per kg.

Turkey led destinations with purchases up 134% to 35.70 million kg, as Iraq dropped 39% to 18.43 million kg and Russia was broadly flat at 16.91 million kg. Tea bags and green tea secured higher dollar prices, while instant tea volumes grew 22.9% in the nine‑month period.

title: Prison population declined by 12% in the September quarter.
body_paragraphs: The Justice Minister told Parliament that inmate numbers fell by 5,068 between July 1 and September 30 as bottlenecks eased, including faster Government Analyst reporting. The department issued 1,506 reports in August and September after staffing was strengthened, and draft amendments would require reports within two months and allow court‑supervised destruction of seized narcotics based on photographic or video records.

title: Zydus Lifesciences and Sunshine Healthcare announced a US$ 20 million pharmaceutical plant in Horana.
body_paragraphs: The joint venture signed with the BOI will develop oral solid dosage forms in its first phase and targets commercial operations in 2028, subject to approvals. The partners said more than 80% of the workforce would be Sri Lankan, with technology transfer and training to support local skills.

title: A policy institute urged continued IMF engagement beyond 2027 to anchor post‑restructuring recovery.
body_paragraphs: The IPS warned of a prolonged debt overhang after market re‑entry, with elevated spreads and limited access compared with pre‑crisis norms. It cautioned against premature commercial borrowing, called for a unified digital public financial management system and proposed an independent fiscal council to strengthen credibility.

title: Heavy rain and landslide risks were forecast for multiple provinces into the weekend.
body_paragraphs: Meteorology advisories warned of showers above 100 mm in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Northern and North‑Western provinces, with thundershowers elsewhere after 1 p.m. The public was urged to watch for lightning, avoid high‑risk slopes and heed warnings as misty conditions were also expected in the early hours.

title: An expert panel was appointed to investigate the death of tusker Kavanthissa and propose welfare procedures.
body_paragraphs: The committee, chaired by a former ministry secretary, was tasked with examining immediate and underlying causes, reviewing any lapses in treatment and drafting standard operating procedures for wild elephant care. A report with recommendations for a national conservation program is due within 30 days.

title: The roads authority moved to gazette eligible provincial and local roads as national highways.
body_paragraphs: The Cabinet spokesperson said applications would be vetted for basic eligibility and technical criteria before gazetting on the recommendation of the takeover committee. The decision followed a July 20, 2026 cabinet‑appointed committee report on transfers, funding and staffing needed to maintain the routes.
